demo_02_degraded_copy.wav.expectation_note: Signal-degraded copy of the target voice, NOT a neural voice clone. AUTHENTIC_TARGET is correct because the speaker is still the target. True acoustic tier is ALLOW (achieved by Layer 5 AASIST with codec augmentation). Legacy Layer 12 AASIST yields CHALLENGE due to sensitivity to saturation. Both ALLOW and CHALLENGE are acceptable across model checkpoints.

demo_03_partial_splice.wav.label: spliced
demo_03_partial_splice.wav.expectation_note: 2026-09-13: expected_tier_aasist widened from CHALLENGE to [CHALLENGE, BLOCK]; the original is kept in expected_tier_aasist_was. With the real ECAPA + AASIST backends this clip scores BLOCK (risk 79.9), and it already did before /analyze began honouring the session BLOCK latch, so that change did not cause it. BLOCK is the correct outcome, not a regression: the 4.0-8.0 s region is a different speaker, and a different person taking over mid-call is the hand-off-to-a-scammer attack the interlock exists to stop. docs/RUNBOOK.md already records partial_splice -> BLOCK under real backends. The invariant that matters for a partly-substituted clip is that it is never ALLOW; that still holds. The stub-backend expected_tier is unchanged.

demo_04_impostor.wav.label: impostor
demo_04_impostor.wav.expectation_note: BLOCK, not just CHALLENGE, because of the deterministic impostor override (RiskConfig.impostor_block_below in config.py): a decisively non-target speaker must engage the interlock even if the weighted fusion alone lands short of the BLOCK line.

demo_05_voice_clone.wav.label: voice_clone

demo_05_voice_clone.wav.expectation_note: First clip in the suite with is_real_clone: true. It is a real ASVspoof5 attack (A30) generated from the bonafide utterance in demo_06_same_speaker_bonafide.wav, and it is what actually exercises the countermeasure. Imported, not authored: see scripts/import_clone_demo.py. The speaker is NOT the enrolled anchor, so the deterministic impostor override also fires — the tier below is driven by identity as well as by the CM. To isolate the CM, enrol the source clip and re-run with that claimed identity; the CM term alone still flips.

demo_06_same_speaker_bonafide.wav.label: clone_source

demo_06_same_speaker_bonafide.wav.expectation_note: The real human whose voice the attack imitates — same speaker, not necessarily the exact source utterance (the eval protocol does not expose that link; see the docstring in this file). Bonafide, hence AUTHENTIC_TARGET as far as the countermeasure is concerned — but a different person from the enrolled anchor, so under claimed_identity=<anchor> the impostor override still returns BLOCK. Enrol this clip as its own identity to compare like with like.
